tools.name: Frying pan (about 24 cm)
tools.note: A big pan helps, cabbage starts bulky.

steps.title: Cut cabbage
points: Tear or cut the cabbage into rough 4 cm squares.

steps.title: Slice sausage
points: Slice the sausages diagonally into coins about 1 cm thick.
Diagonal cuts give each piece more surface to brown.

steps.title: Mix sauce
points: Stir the soy sauce and mustard together in a small bowl.
Set it next to the stove: the end of this recipe goes fast.

steps.title: Brown sausage
points: Spread the sausage coins in one layer and cook about 2 minutes, turning once.
They are ready when both sides have color and the fat starts to run.

steps.title: Add cabbage
points: Pile in all the cabbage. It looks like too much, it isn't.
Let it sit untouched for 1 minute so the bottom layer chars a little.
Toss, then repeat: rest, toss, rest.
steps.hint: Constant stirring steams the cabbage. Letting it sit against the hot pan is what gives you sweet, browned edges.

steps.title: Check cabbage
points: After 3 to 4 minutes it should be glossy and wilted at the edges.
The thick parts should still have some crunch.
Kill the heat there, it keeps cooking in the pan.

steps.title: Add sauce
points: Pour the soy and mustard mixture around the edge of the pan.
Toss everything for 30 seconds, then plate.
Taste before you finish with black pepper: the sausage may carry enough salt on its own.
steps.hint: Sauce poured onto the hot pan edge sizzles and gets aromatic. Poured on the vegetables it just makes them wet.

troubleshooting.solution: The heat was too low or it was stirred nonstop. High heat and patience: let it press against the pan, toss briefly, and repeat. Salting early also draws water out, so season only at the end.
The pieces were too big or the core sneaked in. Thick ribs take longest, cut them thinner than the leaves next time, or give the pan 1 more minute with a splash of water and a brief lid.
Sausages vary a lot. With saltier brands, halve the soy sauce, the mustard alone carries plenty of flavor.
Dijon works, use a little less. Even plain yellow mustard is fine. Or skip it and add a small knob of butter with the soy sauce instead.

troubleshooting.problem: It feels thin as a meal
troubleshooting.solution: Serve it over rice, or push everything aside at the end and fry an egg in the empty half. Both turn it into dinner.
